rows.caveat: The highest LongMemEval_S number known to this project, and the population is stated: "the LongMemEvalS benchmark comprising 500 questions across six categories". It also reproduces arithmetically - the per-category cells the paper reports for Chronos High (98.57 ss-user, 100 ss-assistant, 100 ss-preference, 88.72 multi-session, 95.50 temporal-reasoning, 100 knowledge-update) micro-average over the official counts 70/56/30/133/133/78 to exactly 95.60, which independently confirms n = 500. Backbone is the paper's own definition of "High": "High configurations refer to evaluations with advanced frontier models, such as Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3 Pro"; Chronos Low, on "GPT-4o, or similar", is 92.60 on the same set. The **judge is never named** - the converted text contains no occurrence of "judge" or "grader" - so judge_class is inferred from the backbone class and must be treated as unverified. Chronos is also the published form of M19's mechanism: it "decomposes raw dialogue into subject-verb-object event tuples with resolved datetime ranges" at write time, and reports the events calendar alone as a 58.9% gain over its baseline.
